donor_domain: mathematical statistics: sufficiency of experiments (Fisher-Neyman; Blackwell 1951/1953 comparison of experiments)
donor_source_ids: Wikipedia: Blackwell's informativeness theorem; simple-proof note (ScienceDirect S016517652400630X)
donor_structure: experiment E1 sufficient for E2 iff E2 = garbling of E1 (stochastic transformation); three-way equivalence: sufficiency <=> garbling <=> higher expected utility for every decision problem and prior; minimal sufficient experiment as coarsest sufficient representation
target_structure: a representation (state summary) is sufficient for downstream task decisions iff every alternative representation it replaces is recoverable as a garbling (noise-additive coarsening) of it
mapping: experiment->representation/summary; signal->representation content; garbling stochastic kernel->information-losing re-encoding; decision problem->HSG task; prior->task distribution
preserved_relations: value equivalence: sufficient representation weakly dominates for EVERY decision rule and task distribution
minimal sufficient representation exists as coarsest element
known_broken_relations: Blackwell assumes fixed prior set and single-agent expected utility; HSG verifier/constitution may restrict which decisions are admissible (no direct counterpart)
unknown_correspondences: composition of sufficiency along the time axis (iterated garbling across t) -- donor covers one-shot comparison
assumptions_added: task decisions evaluated under expected loss; representations as Markov kernels from raw state
candidate_theorem: for any two state representations R1, R2: R1 weakly dominates R2 on every burden-bounded task iff R2 is a garbling of R1; hence representation upgrades that are not garbling-reversals have zero value -- direct instantiation of Blackwell 1953
strongest_parent: Blackwell 1951/1953 (sufficiency iff garbling iff value dominance) -- verified via chart retrieval
